_meta.description: Category-level Q10 temperature-coefficient values for a temperature-adjusted shelf-life PREDICTION, layered on top of each commodity's existing typical_ambient_shelf_life_days baseline (see data/commodities.json). The Q10 method is a real, well-established food-science technique for approximating how reaction/spoilage rate scales with temperature: predicted_shelf_life_days = typical_shelf_life_days x Q10^((reference_temperature_c - actual_storage_temp_c) / 10). Deliberately CATEGORY-level, not per-commodity — we don't have per-commodity kinetic measurements, and presenting a fabricated per-commodity precision would overstate what this model actually knows. See engine/shelf_life.py for the calculation and clamping logic.

confidence_levels.medium: Every category here is 'medium': these are literature-typical Q10 ranges for the general food class, not measured kinetic data for any specific commodity in this catalogue. There is no 'high' tier for this feature — we don't have lab-measured, commodity-specific kinetic data, and marking anything here as 'high' confidence would overstate that.

_meta.reference_temperature_note: reference_temperature_c is the temperature each category's EXISTING typical_ambient_shelf_life_days figure is assumed to already represent. For every category except frozen_foods, that's ambient/room temperature (~25C) — the field is literally named 'typical_AMBIENT_shelf_life_days' throughout data/commodities.json, and several commodity notes (e.g. apple, milk_pasteurized) explicitly describe the stated figure as the unrefrigerated/ambient case with refrigeration extending it further. Using a chilled reference temperature (e.g. 4C) for these categories, as a first pass at this feature considered, would have double-counted the temperature effect: it would treat an already-ambient-calibrated number as if it still needed extrapolating up to ambient, silently shrinking the predicted value at the exact temperature (25C) the baseline number is already valid at. frozen_foods is the one deliberate exception — those commodities' notes in commodities.json already state the figure is for FROZEN (-18C) storage, not ambient, so -18C is used as that category's reference point instead.

clamp._note: Prevents a wild storage-temperature input from producing an absurd result. min_days is an absolute floor. max_multiplier caps the prediction at 3x the commodity's own typical_ambient_shelf_life_days midpoint — a temperature far colder than the reference can't imply a near-infinite shelf life extension. When either bound is hit, was_clamped is reported explicitly rather than silently returning the capped number as if it were the raw model output.

fresh_fruit._source_note: Fresh produce: fast-spoiling, biologically active (respiration-driven) — literature-typical Q10 for produce commonly cited in the 2.0-2.5 range.

fresh_vegetable._source_note: Same reasoning as fresh_fruit — fast-spoiling, biologically active fresh produce.

dairy._source_note: Microbially fast-spoiling at ambient temperature, consistent with this catalogue's dairy commodities already showing very short (<1 day) typical ambient shelf life.

meat_fish._source_note: The fastest-spoiling category in this catalogue at ambient temperature (hours-scale for several commodities) — placed at the top of the fresh-produce/dairy/meat Q10 range for that reason.

dry_goods_grains._source_note: Slow, mostly moisture/oxidation-driven spoilage rather than active microbial/respiration spoilage — literature-typical Q10 for dry staples commonly cited in the 1.3-1.5 range.

spices._source_note: Very low moisture, aroma/oxidation-driven degradation rather than spoilage in the microbial sense — placed at the low end of the slow-kinetics range.

nuts_dried_fruits._source_note: Oxidative-rancidity-driven (see this catalogue's own material notes on nuts), same general slow-kinetics family as dry goods/spices but faster due to higher fat content.

bakery._source_note: Mold growth and staling are temperature-sensitive but not as fast-kinetics as active microbial spoilage in fresh produce/dairy/meat.

ready_to_eat_snacks._source_note: Fried/oxidation-driven degradation, grouped with bakery per similar literature-typical Q10 range.

beverages._source_note: This catalogue's beverages are largely dairy- or fresh-juice-based with short typical ambient shelf life — treated with the same fast-kinetics Q10 as dairy.

frozen_foods._source_note: Reference temperature is -18C (standard freezer temperature), matching the frozen-storage assumption already documented on this catalogue's frozen_foods commodities — NOT 25C, since their typical_ambient_shelf_life_days figure represents frozen storage, not literal room temperature. Q10 placed at the fast end: once warmed toward/above freezing, frozen-food quality loss is commonly cited as following similarly fast temperature-doubling kinetics to fresh perishables.
